_: The four close-up cameras that show whether a painted pattern is doing anything: a pot, two deck
chairs and a table, two boulders, and the terrace rail. Each case is run twice — as built, and
with the four patterned materials forced back to one flat byte each — and what the two runs differ
by at a pick is what the pattern is worth on the screen.
Every case carries float=1: the walking code eases the visitor onto the ground under them every
frame, so a camera aimed at a chair seat a metre off the ground is lifted to eye height and the
chair leaves the bottom of the picture. That was happening here unnoticed, and the picks printed

cases.name: flat as it was
cases.js: const flat={wood:[150,104,62],pot:[176,118,78],stone:[138,130,118],soil:[72,54,38]};const conv=(b)=>{const c=b/255;return c<=0.04045?c/12.92:Math.pow((c+0.055)/1.055,2.4);};for(const k in flat){const m=mats[k];m.albedoTexture=null;m.bumpTexture=null;m.albedoColor=new BABYLON.Color3(conv(flat[k][0]),conv(flat[k][1]),conv(flat[k][2]));}
